top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn; B038) is my top choice on the common criteria. It combines new measurement, a transparent local-labour-market design and a durable finding of concentrated, persistent adjustment costs to trade and technology exposure. It has more than a decade of replication, critique and extension behind it, so durability can be judged. Round 2 narrowed the citation to the empirical exposure-and-adjustment evidence and left out the task-framework lineage, which cannot be credited to this trio. That also settled Dorn over Katz as the third name. The shift-share debate and the contested size of the effects lower confidence in the magnitudes, not in the qualitative finding. P003 (B002) is second because its measurement and design are strong, but restricted data and the short record of the long-run causal estimates lower its maturity. P005 (B041) comes next. It is a clear mechanism, but the credit of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum cannot be honoured, and Helpman's credit is shared with P004. P002 (B001) is mature and cleanly attributed, but its empirical reach is indirect and earlier game-theory prizes cover nearby ground. P004 (B013) has clean attribution, but the record of the specific predictions is mixed. All five proposals are preferable to no award, so P000 is last. I do not rest this ranking on support counts, and I recognise that my macro and firm-dynamics background may bias me.
recusal_note: No connection to any credited laureate on P001-P005 is apparent from the profile. My frequent co-authors Krusell and Hassler are committee members and are not credited on any proposal. Peter Klenow, a long-time co-author, is credited only on B023, which is not on the slate. I disclose my collaboration with Aghion, Bergeaud, Klenow and Li on creative destruction, my co-authorship of the Ekonomisk Debatt summaries of the 2024 and 2025 prizes, and the weak evidence that I helped draft the 2025 Scientific Background. None of these touches a 2026 proposal. Ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
